book: The Ladder of Divine Ascent — Selections

1: [Ladder, Step 1 — On the renunciation of the world]

As the tree is known by its fruit, so the renunciation of the world is known by freedom from care. He who has truly left all things is not the one who has given away the most, but the one who has stopped weighing them — and this one has wings, though he walk.

The beginning of the beginning is the courage to be despised. For the world honours the climber, and the ladder of God is climbed by going down — and the first step down is to be thought nothing of, and to be glad of it.

Obedience is a yoke willingly taken, and in the taking the burden is lifted. The novice who says yes is not losing his will; he is laying down the heaviest thing he carries, and the elders call that thing 'I'.
[Ladder, Step 4 — The letter and the spirit]

He who obeys in the letter only is a hired servant; he who obeys in the spirit is a son. The difference is not in the commandment but in the heart — and God reads the heart and leaves the letter for the record.
2: Repentance is the daughter of hope and the refusal to despair. It is not the weeping for what is done, but the washing of the eyes so that what is not yet done may be seen coming — and seen, it loses half its power.

Some say that tears are the grave of sins. I say they are the baptism of the old man, and the coffin of the new. For the tear that falls in truth falls on the seed, and what rises from it is not sorrow but harvest.

Blessed is he who weeps for himself daily, for he is watering a garden no one else can see. And the garden is his own heart, and what grows there feeds the whole neighbourhood, though they never know the gardener.
3: Discernment is the eye of the soul, and it is sharpened by humility and dulled by haste. He who judges quickly sees the surface; he who waits sees the root; and the root of nearly everything is fear, and fear is answered by love.
[Ladder, Step 30 — On faith, hope and love]

And now these three remain — faith, hope and love. Faith is the wing, hope is the breath, and love is the fire; and of the three, love alone burns without consuming, and it is the ladder's top, and it is also the ground the ladder stands on.

The angelic ladder is set up on earth, and its feet are in the dust, and its top leans on heaven — and the climber who reaches the top finds that he is carrying it, and those below are climbing his shoulders. This is the meaning of the saints: they are not the destination; they are the rungs.
